rationale.conceptual: The method (DFT+CHE) is well-established in electrocatalysis but requires careful implementation: selecting RPBE functional, Vanderbilt ultrasoft pseudopotentials, plane-wave cutoff, free-energy corrections (ZPE, entropy), and employing the CHE framework. It’s not a simple plug-and-play model; the combination of surface science and electrochemical free-energy diagramming makes it a multi-part documented algorithm that demands domain understanding.
rationale.execution: Reproducing the result involves a multi-stage pipeline: (1) building a Cu(211) slab, (2) running DFT geometry optimizations and vibrational frequencies for clean surface and adsorbates (CH2OH*, OH*), (3) extracting free-energy corrections, (4) deriving aqueous methanediol free energy from standard data and hydration equilibrium, (5) constructing CHE diagrams and computing limiting potentials. This entails non-trivial tooling (Dacapo or alternative DFT code, pseudopotential handling), data assembly, and several load-bearing handoffs, making it a lengthy, orchestrated workflow.
